note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's 1897 original description (in Latin), original name Eutermes chrysopleura n. sp., a short account in the preliminary notice 'Neue Termiten aus West-Afrika' with only one paragraph on the female alate; the original states that the wings of the specimen are missing (ale desunt) and that the number of antennal segments was queried by the author himself (13?); no measurements are given. Type locality Victoria, Cameroon, collected by Buchholz in September 1873 (month 9), specimen in the Greifswald Museum.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is closest to E. latifrons but differs in the golden-yellow long pubescence on the sides of the body (female), the pale yellowish white legs and antennae, and the pale brown sternites.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate (female): body flattened; head, thorax and abdominal dorsum dark brown, the sides of the body densely covered with golden-yellow pubescence; legs and antennae pale yellowish white, without any brown; sternites pale brown, slightly paler in the middle; antennae 13-segmented (recorded in the original as 13?, doubtful); wings missing in this specimen, so neither venation nor measurements can be given.
